what_changed_today: PRICE BROKE BELOW THE SMA CLUSTER: close 7,457.69 (~-1.0% vs prior 7,533.77) has now slipped beneath both the 20-day and the flattening 50-day (~7,465), the first clean loss of the moving-average support that held through the multi-week grind at the swing high.

MONTE CARLO FLIPPED HARD DOWN-FIRST: adjusted prob_up_first collapsed to 26.5% (from 63.4% prior), with 73.5% down-first and median days downside 2d vs upside 10d — the most bearish near-term skew of the recovery, failing all regime thresholds.
VIX ROSE OFF THE FLOOR TO 18.77 (from ~16.5 area): volatility pushed to the top of the standard operating band and back to its 50-day MA, ending the benign sub-16 backdrop of prior sessions.
ERP CUSHION AT ZERO: forward earnings yield 5.02% versus the 10-year at 4.541% leaves the equity risk premium at ~0.0%, pinned at the very bottom of the valuation-ceiling band.

PRICE LOST THE 23.6% FIB: close 7,457.69 is now below the 23.6% fib (7,498) that had capped and then supported the grind, sitting between the 23.6% and 38.2% fib (7,448) with the downside target at 7,448.
narrative_summary: SPX fell ~1.0% to 7,457.69, decisively breaking below the 20/50-day SMA cluster and the 23.6% fib (7,498) after weeks of tagging and stalling at the 6/15 swing high (7,578). The bull skeleton is still structurally intact (50d > rising 200d, +6.7% over the 200-day) but is clearly maturing: Monte Carlo has flipped hard down-first (73.5%, median 2 days to the 7,448 downside target), VIX has risen to 18.77 at its 50-day MA, and the ERP cushion has evaporated to ~0.0% against a valuation ceiling. Breadth (McClellan ~900) and net new highs (~2.0) still refuse to confirm, so the posture stays defensive: hold, protect capital, and watch the 7,448–7,408 fib/ERP-floor confluence for a first re-entry test.
open_questions: Does the loss of the 20/50-day SMA cluster and the 23.6% fib mark the start of a genuine correction toward the 38.2%/50% fib zone (7,448–7,408), or a shallow shake-out that reclaims quickly?
Will McClellan breadth (~900, near its lows) and net new 52-week highs (~2.0) finally deteriorate to confirm the price weakness, or stabilize?
Does VIX at its 50-day MA (18.77) resolve into a genuine volatility expansion, or fade back below 16 as prior spikes did?

conflicting_evidence.bullish_read: The primary trend remains up: 50d above a rising 200d, +6.7% over the 200-day, Low exhaustion and full drift — a down-first skew is a tactical pullback within an intact bull, and the 60-day drift path still projects back to ~7,572.

conflicting_evidence.framework_rule: Never use the Monte Carlo output in isolation; interpret it through Structural Bias. A close below the 20-day SMA after an extended advance is a regime shift, not just a normal dip.

primary_tension: A structurally intact but maturing bull skeleton (50d > rising 200d, +6.7% over the 200-day, Low exhaustion, full drift) is colliding with a decisive short-term breakdown — price lost the 20/50-day SMA cluster and the 23.6% fib, Monte Carlo flipped hard down-first (73.5%, median 2 days to 7,448), VIX rose to its 50-day MA, and a zero-cushion ERP at the valuation ceiling — while breadth and credit still refuse to confirm the recovery.
